summary: folder-lint preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundle
details: The package declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases, extracts it to a temp directory, marks it executable, and uses it to execute a shipped ~728KB Bun-compiled CJS bundle (`math_init.js`) at the tarball root. The bundle is heavily obfuscated (rotated string/constant array `n7gIxM`, `WV8StW` array-shuffling decoder, dynamic string reconstruction) and is not referenced by the package's declared `main` entry (`lib/index.js`). The package advertises itself as a folder-structure linter authored by ServiceTitan with homepage `github.com/servicetitan/folder-lint` and an Apache-2.0 license, but the upstream project ships neither a preinstall hook nor a Bun bundle, and the README is an unpopulated `TODO: description` stub. Fetching an alternate language runtime purely to execute an opaque obfuscated payload at install time — while impersonating an unrelated legitimate publisher — is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern; the Bun execution path evades Node-based inspection and the payload's behavior cannot be inferred from its advertised purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
